note: PROVISIONAL. Derived from container runs of the SO-04 completion harness plus a margin. Not hardware evidence, and not a program-plan section 8 target: those are unchanged. Read only by the service-objective harness and validator; the core never reads this file and nothing here changes when or how a lease is released.

basis.method: py/azazel_edge/service_objectives/so04_rollback_completion.py on main after #439: real azazel-edge-core daemon (Edge defaults, enforcement off), owned nft rule installed per lease, monotonic lease deadlines (CLOCK_BOOTTIME, every sample expiry_clock monotonic), start and end both read on CLOCK_BOOTTIME, half the leases expiring under the harness's eve_flood load (2000 EVE alerts/s); docker --cap-add NET_ADMIN on colima, aarch64
basis.margin_rule: twice the max observed, rounded up to the next 1000 ms
basis.clock_stability: wall_clock_stable_during_run was unmet in 1 of the 3 runs (wall-minus-monotonic drift -108.6 ms against a 50 ms tolerance; the colima VM's wall clock was adjusted during the run). Elapsed times are on CLOCK_BOOTTIME and every lease expired on its monotonic deadline, so the drift does not enter them, but the run is not clean. An earlier set of 3 runs (before #439, start mapped from the wall deadline, drift -111 to -206 ms as found in review, also unmet) gave maxima of 2446.3 ms (isolate) and 2618.3 ms (redirect); it is superseded and not used here.

undeclared.reason: No completion was observed, so there is nothing to derive a bound from. In 150 container samples with the lease's TBF qdisc installed, every rollback attempt ended release_attempt_failed with 'tc ownership handle exists with unexpected TBF parameters': iproute2 6.15 'tc -j qdisc show' reports rate/burst/lat under 'options', and the core's readback (release.rs tbf_parameters_match) looks for them at the top level. Until that is fixed and measured, throttle declares no bound and the SO-04 completion half stays not_measurable.
